summary: Existing products implement pieces of the loop: bidirectional Git synchronization, UI-to-pull-request write-back, source-built portals, and model-as-code views. No listed tool independently performs semantic, conflict-aware reconciliation across code, runtime, decisions, and a companion.

items.text: GitBook Git Sync supports bidirectional synchronization between GitBook content and a GitHub or GitLab repository, with changes from either side represented through commits and reviewable branches.

Decap CMS Editorial Workflow turns browser edits into Git branches and pull requests with draft, review, and ready states; merging updates the repository, making companion-originated write-back reviewable.
Backstage TechDocs builds repository documentation in CI and serves the resulting site in the catalog, supplying the artifact-to-companion half with explicit source ownership and rebuild history.

Structurizr's versionable DSL produces multiple diagrams, documentation, and decision views from one architecture model, reducing internal drift among companion representations while keeping changes reviewable as text.
GitHub Actions can trigger reconciliation on repository events or schedules and can require generated-view drift checks before merge, turning freshness from a promise into a repeatable workflow.
